name: backend-api
summary: Backend/API structure with API surface, services, models, repositories, config, and tests.
dependency_direction: api -> services -> repositories/external adapters -> models. API handlers should stay thin.

folders.responsibility: HTTP/API entry points, routing, request/response boundaries.
folders.allowed: Route handlers, controllers, request validation boundaries.
folders.avoid: Business logic and direct database implementation details.

folders.responsibility: Business logic and application use cases.
folders.allowed: Use case orchestration, domain workflows, transaction boundaries.

folders.responsibility: Persistence and external data source adapters.
folders.allowed: Database queries, storage adapters, external API data adapters.

folders.responsibility: Domain models, schemas, DTOs, and validation types.

folders.allowed: Typed config, env validation with placeholders.
Service tests, API tests, repository tests with fixtures.
folders.avoid: Manual-only validation for auth, data, or payment behavior.

rules: Do not expose model/API provider keys to clients.
Keep API handlers thin and service logic testable.
Use security-focused review appropriate to the changed auth, payment, secret, or data-access boundary; use a specialized Skill only when it is exposed and useful.
validation: Inspect project scripts before running tests or migrations.
Do not run database migrations without explicit confirmation.
Choose security scanning, threat modeling, or project-native checks according to the changed auth, payment, secret, or data-access surface and the capabilities already available.
